en: When Taal Volcano erupts, wearing an N95 mask protects your lungs from inhaling dangerous volcanic ash that can cause severe breathing problems.
After a typhoon floods Manila, wading in dirty floodwater can cause leptospirosis from rat urine, so always wash your feet thoroughly with soap.
Living near the West Valley Fault in Metro Manila means practicing earthquake drills and knowing your local evacuation route to stay safe during tremors.
During the rainy season in Cebu, emptying stagnant water from old tires prevents Aedes mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue fever to your family.
Climbing Mount Pulag in Benguet requires thick jackets because temperatures can drop below freezing, causing dangerous hypothermia if your clothes get wet.
Swimming at Siargao beaches requires watching for rip currents, which are strong underwater rivers that can pull you out to sea if you panic.
During the extreme summer heat in Pampanga, drinking plenty of water and wearing a hat prevents heatstroke, a dangerous condition where your body overheats.
Exploring the Puerto Princesa Underground River requires wearing a helmet to protect your head from low, jagged limestone stalactites hanging from the dark ceiling.
Avoid swimming in freshwater bodies in Samar to prevent schistosomiasis, a disease caused by parasitic worms that penetrate your skin in contaminated water.
After heavy rains hit Mount Pinatubo, staying away from riverbanks is crucial because loose volcanic ash forms fast, deadly mudflows called lahars.
If a thunderstorm strikes while you are in the Bicol region, avoid standing under tall trees to prevent being hit by a deadly lightning bolt.
When snorkeling in Tubbataha Reef, wear water shoes to protect your feet from sharp coral cuts and venomous stonefish hiding on the sandy ocean floor.
